Wouldn't recommend this game in its current state unfortunately. I played this with the Valve Index controllers and unfortunately the controls are buggy at best. I had to disable my touchpads/scrollwheels just to get the motion controls to work comfortably, and after that i had a bug where shaking my controllers would switch the weapons. It's a neat mechanic but unfortunately it fails when youre quickly drawing back an arrow or quickly swish-stabbing an enemy. The game concept is neat but a lot is unexplained properly and prone to error in terms of controls and system stuff. 

IF they fixed their controls and made movement more fluid (you can only move forward or back, either from a headset pov or a controller pov, which is terrible), then this game would actually be pretty fun to play with other people, provided they added more interesting content, but the 'amount' of content in the game is actually just heavily repeated and grindy to actually get to.

Would not recommend: 4/10.

I got Trickster VR back when it first released into Early Access back in 2016, and from what I tried I was excited but wanted to wait for the full product to be finished. Well even at "full release 1.0" it still had issues, so I waited longer. Now it's clear that it's just not going to be what I had hoped for.

The game itself would be good if it were technically sound. My only issue is the progressive degradation of the visuals, with framerate drops and visual smearing after the game has been open for less than one mission. I have my FPS showing and it is locked at 90 and all my other more demanding VR games run fine, but less than 15 minutes in Trickster get to the point of nausea. There's a lot of good gameplay stuff to potentially talk about but it's not even worth mentioning at this point.

No proper collision - Your weapons and attacks can just phase through walls and enemies a majority of the time and they are capable of swinging through your shield. Player character is able to walk through rocks and walls and enemies
No control scheme - I looked but did not spend too much time looking for a control scheme, it says there is a special move for each weapon but I could not get it to activate on any weapon with any button or motion combination.
Poorly optimized procedural generation - You can almost always seem the seams of the games 'set pieces', frequently "tripping" over them as your movement stutters briefly or you downright get stuck on them
Large floating rocks drift around the game world but frequently come into the playing field obscuring vision or covering enemies as they run toward you.

I tend to be a selfish Steamite, I play games and either enjoy them or not, but typically keep my opinions to myself.  However, for this game, I'm taking the time to say something and provide a review.

First of all, let's just set the stage for what I have to say: This game has to be one of the most best titles (for VR) that I've played if you care about the following:
1. Purely for fun with a extremely low learning curve (for evenings you just want to spend time with family or friends, having a good time)
2. Drop-in play potential is, by far, one of the best of any title (VR and non-VR) that I've ever played (for those of us who just want to get in, have a drink with family or friends, and enjoy a bit of ongoing adventure)
3. The game mechanics are entirely intuitive
4. Bow usage is not punishing with accuracy requirements that really never fits VR well.  The accuracy is well tuned to balance some semblance of enjoyable realistic combat with a 'just have fun' attitude.

So, if you are a player who likes to put their 'try hard' efforts on hold now and again, then gather your group, crack open a bottle of your preferred alcohol (tequilla for me thank you very much), and jump in.  You simply can't miss with this game's fun to cost quotient.

Congratulations!  Another big fail in VR movement!

I understand.  Why allow us to move with the left thumbstick and turn with the right thumbstick?  Why give us what we want?  Why let us move and turn the same way we've been doing for 22 years since Goldeneye?  To hell with us, right?  You know better than us, of course!

In an ocean of horrible VR movement schemes, this stands out as one of the singularly dumbest things I've ever encountered.  You can teleport or you can teleport.  Those are your only real options.

There is a smooth locomotion option titled "Walk," but then there's no control for turning whatsoever!  Obviously that's awful and ridiculous.  Why would you POSSIBLY make it that way???  So you're stuck with in real life turning only if you want smooth locomotion, right?  Yes, but it gets even worse.  You can't backpedal either!  Every single direction on the left thumbstick makes you mindlessly walk forward.  This means that if you're surrounded and need to back up, you have to physically turn 180° IRL then you can do your zombie locomotion, unable to attack the throng following you while you retreat.  It is the dumbest and most debilitating thing to do to your own players who just want to move smoothly like in every first person game they've ever played in their lives.

In addition to the "Teleport" movement option, there is a "Twin Stick" option though.  That should be great, right?  The devs do know that it's possible to move with the left thumbstick and turn with the right after all!!  Well, you can only use teleportation with Twin Stick.  A big FU to anyone who doesn't get motion sick in VR.  I mean, why would you want to cater to such evil people as those who use VR regularly and are well suited to it?

Worry not, oh noble developers.  This evil smooth locomotor will never sully another game you make with his purchase.

I wanted to like this game. I saw the good reviews, some solid gameplay, and was excited that it wasn't just another 3-4 hour story. Unfortunately, some of the core mechanics just make the game frustrating to play.

First, let's talk a little bit about hitboxes. Where IS my hitbox? Arrow looks like it's flying over my head? Headshot. Dodge incoming fireball? Nope just kidding. And then there's the shield. This is one of the largest shields (visually) that I've seen in a vr game. And yet it feels like the hitbox is smaller than any other shield I've ever used. Also why even have a shield when enemies can just walk up to you and swing sight through it. Also why can enemies walk into me? I can't hit them when they are inside me but they can hit me.

Next, up is melee combat. I don't like the hitstun. At first it was satisfying but after a bit it just feels awkward; especially when using dual weapons. Also what is up with armor hit boxes. Sometimes I swing straight through their armor and it's fine, other times I sing at flesh and bounce. What gives? Also did i mention that the shield sucks? Because the shield sucks.

Ranged combat is actually pretty good. Nothing to complain about here. Carry on.

Movement also sucks. I never feel like I can move where I need to mid combat especially because moving side to side or backwards is annoying to do yet is integral to successfully dodging attacks. Not to mention that it's very restrictive in where I can go. If I want to jump off of a cliff to drop attacks some orcs I should be able to do so. I'm fine with invisible walls on the stage bounds preventing me from falling into the abyss but why do they also need to be at the staircase preventing me from taking a shortcut.

Options, or rather, the lack thereof. There need to be more options for UI adjustments and movement options. I don't want to swipe to turn my camera, I want to physically press a button. It works correctly far more often and can be done faster. Also can I get an option to remove the blood staying the screen whenever I get hit? It's incredibly distracting and makes the punishment for getting clipped by janky hitboxes all the more punishing now that I can't even see the enemies / attacks. 

I can't recommend this game in its current state. It has tons of potential but is just far too frustrating to actually play.

Tremendous fun, even in single-player. All missions are quick and straight-forward, weapons are unlockable and upgradeable and the enemies come complete with readily-identifiable classes and discoverable weak points. 

Between the running commentary, the uncluttered aesthetic and the generous VR comfort options, this is an easy recommendation for anyone new to VR, those on a tight schedule, or simply archers who like to shoot their arrows into orcs. 

You will, however, need to cultivate a bit of skill if you want to throw things, or use magic (such is life).

For the downside: The gamemodes are few and the terrain unvaried, but that doesn’t bother me. I would prefer more story elements. Collision detection for the player’s own weapons would help with immersion - I keep feeling compelled to bang my sword against my shield before storming into the next skirmish. The main improvement would be in clearer menu navigation and remapping for every control, to take full advantage of the options available.

Due to the nature of the procedural generation algorithm, sometimes odd visual effects occur, or orcs might get stuck on rocks, but the only real difficulties I’ve experienced have been due to Steam VR’s implementation. For that, the developer has been attentive and supportive and resolved the issue entirely by removing Steam VR from my experience.
